MA.q: A nursing student reads 45 pages of a pharmacology textbook in 1 hour 15 minutes. At the same rate, how long will it take her to read 162 pages?
MA.w: 1 hour 15 minutes = 75 minutes. Set up 45/75 = 162/t. Cross-multiply: 45t = 12,150, so t = 270 minutes = 4 hours 30 minutes.

n.1: This uses 1 hour instead of 1 hour 15 minutes for the 45 pages.
n.2: This finds 4.5 hours and then reads the 0.5 as 50 minutes. Half an hour is 30 minutes.
n.3: This writes 1 hour 15 minutes as 1.15 hours. Fifteen minutes is 0.25 hour.

MA.q: Which military time is a quarter past 4 in the afternoon?
MA.w: A quarter past 4 p.m. is 4:15 p.m. Add 12 to the hour: 1615.

n.0: 0415 is 4:15 a.m.; afternoon hours need 12 added.
n.2: This adds 10 to the hour; 1415 is 2:15 p.m.
n.3: 1645 is 4:45 p.m., a quarter to 5; a quarter past is 15 minutes.

MA.q: A dietitian estimates a man's resting calorie needs with the expression 10w + 6.25h - 5a + 5, where w is weight in kilograms, h is height in centimeters, and a is age in years. What value does the expression give for w = 80, h = 175, and a = 40?

n.1: This leaves off the constant + 5 at the end of the expression.
n.2: This adds 5a instead of subtracting it: the expression has - 5a, so 200 is taken away.
n.3: This treats the final + 5 as - 5, which makes the result 10 lower.

MA.q: An order is for 125 mcg of a medication. Tablets on hand contain 0.25 mg each. How many tablets should be given? (1 mg = 1,000 mcg)
MA.w: Convert: 125 mcg ÷ 1,000 = 0.125 mg. Desired ÷ have: 0.125 ÷ 0.25 = 0.5 tablet.

n.0: This converts 125 mcg to 0.0125 mg, moving the decimal point four places.
n.1: This inverts the ratio: 0.25 ÷ 0.125 = 2.
n.3: This converts 125 mcg to 1.25 mg, moving the decimal point only two places.

MA.q: Write 84/36 as a mixed number in lowest terms.

n.0: 2 1/7 simplifies to 7/3 first and then writes the remainder 1 over the numerator 7 instead of the denominator 3.
n.1: 2 1/6 simplifies 12/36 by dividing 12 by 12 but 36 by 6; both terms must be divided by the same number.
n.2: 2 12/36 has the right value, but the stem asks for lowest terms and 12/36 still shares a factor of 12.

MA.q: Each tablet of a vitamin supplement contains 0.05 milligram of vitamin B12, and a patient takes 3 tablets a day. The dietitian's log records vitamin doses in micrograms. How many micrograms of vitamin B12 does the patient take each day?
MA.w: Daily amount = 3 × 0.05 mg = 0.15 mg. Milligrams to micrograms: multiply by 1,000, so 0.15 mg = 150 mcg.

n.0: This converts one tablet correctly (0.05 mg = 50 mcg) but does not multiply by the 3 tablets taken each day.
n.1: This multiplies by 100 instead of 1,000; 1 mg = 1,000 mcg.
n.3: This multiplies by 10,000, moving the decimal point four places instead of three.

MA.q: A pharmacy sells the same brand of vitamin gummies in four bottle sizes. Which bottle has the lowest price per gummy?
MA.w: Unit price = price ÷ quantity. $6.08 ÷ 32 = $0.19 per gummy, the lowest of $0.21, $0.19, $0.205, and $0.22.

n.0: $5.04 ÷ 24 = $0.21 per gummy, which is more than $0.19.
n.1: This is the largest bottle, but $8.20 ÷ 40 = $0.205 per gummy, which is more than $0.19.
n.2: This has the lowest total price, but $3.52 ÷ 16 = $0.22 per gummy, the highest unit price.

MA.q: A specimen cup holds 0.12 L. How many milliliters does it hold?
MA.w: 1 L = 1,000 mL, and milliliters are smaller, so multiply: 0.12 × 1,000 = 120 mL.

n.1: This multiplies by 10, the deciliter factor.
n.2: This multiplies by 10,000, one place too far.
n.3: This multiplies by 100, the centiliter factor.

MA.q: A topical cream contains 0.25% active ingredient. Which decimal is equal to 0.25%?
MA.w: Percent to decimal: divide by 100 (move the point 2 places left). 0.25% = 0.0025.

n.0: 0.00025 moves the decimal point 3 places left; 0.00025 = 0.025%.
n.1: 0.25 drops the percent sign without dividing by 100; 0.25 = 25%.
n.2: 0.025 moves the decimal point only 1 place left; 0.025 = 2.5%.

MA.q: Maya has $200. She spends $46.75, $38.09 and $112.60. How much money does she have left?

n.0: $115.16 subtracts only the first two purchases.
n.1: $3.56 forgets to reduce the ones digit to 9 after borrowing from it.
n.2: $197.44 is the amount spent, not the amount left.

MA.q: A nursing program needs lab coats for 150 students and 8 instructors. It already has 10 new coats in storage, and more coats come only in boxes of 12. What is the least number of boxes the program must order so that everyone gets a coat?
MA.w: Coats needed: 150 + 8 = 158. Subtract the 10 in storage: 158 - 10 = 148. Boxes: 148 ÷ 12 = 12.33. Twelve boxes hold only 144 coats, so round up to 13 boxes (156 coats, enough for the 148 still needed).

n.0: 12 boxes rounds 12.33 down; 12 boxes plus storage give 144 + 10 = 154 coats, 4 short.
n.1: 11 boxes subtracts the 8 instructors instead of adding them (150 - 8 - 10 = 132, and 132 ÷ 12 = 11).
n.3: 14 boxes ignores the 10 coats in storage (158 ÷ 12 = 13.17, rounded up), so it orders one box too many.

MA.q: An infusion runs at 80 mL per hour from 9:30 a.m. to 3:45 p.m. How many milliliters are infused?
MA.w: Elapsed time: 9:30 a.m. to 3:30 p.m. is 6 hours, plus 15 minutes = 6.25 hours. Volume: 80 × 6.25 = 500 mL.

n.0: This writes 6 hours 15 minutes as 6.15 hours. Fifteen minutes is 0.25 hour.
n.1: This counts the time as 5 hours 45 minutes (5.75 × 80). From 9:30 a.m. to 3:45 p.m. is 6 hours 15 minutes.
n.3: This uses 6 hours and leaves out the extra 15 minutes.

MA.q: A cafeteria worker pours a 6.3-liter container of soup into bowls that each hold 0.18 liter. How many bowls can be filled?
MA.w: Move both decimal points 2 places right so the divisor is a whole number: 6.3 ÷ 0.18 = 630 ÷ 18 = 35 bowls.

n.0: 1.134 is 6.3 × 0.18; finding how many portions fit requires division.
n.2: 350 moves the decimal point in 6.3 three places but in 0.18 only two.
n.3: 3.5 moves the decimal point in 0.18 two places but in 6.3 only one place.

MA.q: After 65% of a bottle of hand sanitizer has been used, 210 mL remain. How many milliliters did the full bottle hold? Enter the number of milliliters.

tr.323.08: Divided 210 by 0.65; the 210 mL left is 35% of the bottle, not 65%.
tr.136.5: Found 65% of 210 instead of the whole bottle.

MA.w: If 65% is used, 100% - 65% = 35% remains. 210 mL is 35% of the bottle, so the whole = 210 ÷ 0.35 = 600 mL. Check: 0.35 × 600 = 210.

MA.q: A home health visit lasts 105 minutes. The agency bills $40 per hour. What is the charge for the visit?

n.0: This rounds the visit up to 2 hours before billing.
n.1: This writes 1 h 45 min as 1.45 h; 45 minutes is 0.75 hour.
n.2: This reads 105 minutes as 1.05 hours, as if an hour had 100 minutes.

MA.q: Four race times, in minutes, are listed in different forms. Which list shows the times in descending order (greatest to least)?

n.0: 2.205 is less than 2 1/4 = 2.250, so it must come after 2 1/4.
n.1: This list is in ascending order (least to greatest), the reverse of what is asked.
n.3: 2.205 is not the greatest; having more digits does not make a decimal larger (2.205 < 2.3).

MA.q: A physical therapist records that a patient's forward reach improved by 2 3/8 inches. Write this length as an exact decimal. Enter the number of inches only.

tr.0.375: Gave only the fraction part and dropped the 2 whole inches.

MA.w: Divide the fraction part: 3 ÷ 8 = 0.375. Add the whole number: 2 + 0.375 = 2.375 inches.

MA.q: Which temperature reading is the highest?

n.1: 101.3 °F = 38.5 °C, which is below 38.6 °C.

MA.q: A patient fell asleep at 10:50 p.m. and woke at 6:25 a.m. How long did the patient sleep?
MA.w: 10:50 p.m. to midnight is 1 h 10 min. Midnight to 6:25 a.m. is 6 h 25 min. Total: 7 h 35 min.

n.0: This counts from 11:00 p.m. and leaves out the 10 minutes before it.
n.2: This finds 2400 - 2250 = 150 and reads it as 1 h 50 min instead of 1 h 10 min.
n.3: This subtracts 6:25 from 10:50 as if both times were in the same half of the day.

MA.q: A $120 stethoscope is marked 25% off. At checkout, a coupon takes an additional 10% off the sale price. What is the final price of the stethoscope, before tax?
MA.w: Successive discounts multiply. After 25% off: 120 × 0.75 = $90. After another 10% off: 90 × 0.90 = $81. The total discount is 32.5%, not 35%.

n.1: This applies the 10% coupon but not the 25% markdown.
n.2: This adds the discounts to get 35% off. The 10% applies to the $90 sale price, not to $120.
n.3: This applies the 25% markdown but not the 10% coupon.

MA.q: An audit of patient charts on a unit found that 5/6 of the charts were fully complete. Which percentage is equivalent to 5/6?
MA.w: 5 ÷ 6 = 0.8333..., a repeating decimal. As a percent this is 83.333...% = 83 1/3%. Check: 1/6 = 16 2/3%, and 5 × 16 2/3% = 83 1/3%.

n.1: 120% = 6/5. This divides the denominator by the numerator.
n.2: 8 1/3% = 0.08333..., which moves the decimal point in 0.8333... only 1 place right.
n.3: 62 1/2% is the benchmark for 5/8, not 5/6.

MA.q: A child's dose is 7.5 mL of liquid medicine. The parent has a measuring spoon marked in teaspoons. How many teaspoons should be given?

n.0: This divides by 30 mL, the value of a fluid ounce (7.5 ÷ 30 = 1/4).
n.1: This divides by 15 mL, the value of a tablespoon (7.5 ÷ 15 = 1/2).
n.3: This divides by 3, the number of teaspoons in a tablespoon, which is not a milliliter factor.

MA.q: Evaluate 50 - 2 × (3 + 4)².
MA.w: Parentheses: 3 + 4 = 7. Exponent: 7² = 49. Multiply: 2 × 49 = 98. Subtract: 50 - 98 = -48.

n.0: -146 multiplies 2 × 7 before squaring: 50 - 14²; the exponent comes before multiplication.
n.1: 2,352 subtracts 50 - 2 first: 48 × 49; multiplication comes before subtraction.
n.2: 0 squares each term inside the parentheses (9 + 16 = 25) instead of squaring the sum 7.

MA.q: A nutrition study records each participant's fluid intake in deciliters. One participant drank 1.8 liters of water during the day. How many deciliters should the researcher record for this participant?
MA.w: Deci- means one tenth, so 1 L = 10 dL. 1.8 × 10 = 18 dL.

n.0: This uses 100 per liter, which is the centiliter factor (1 L = 100 cL).
n.1: This uses 1,000 per liter, which is the milliliter factor (1 L = 1,000 mL).
n.3: This divides by 10. A deciliter is smaller than a liter, so the number of deciliters must be larger.

MA.q: Convert 35.5 °C to degrees Fahrenheit.

n.0: This multiplies by 9/5 but leaves out adding 32.
n.1: This multiplies by 5/9 (the Fahrenheit-to-Celsius factor) and then adds 32.
n.3: This rounds 35.5 °C up to 36 °C before converting; round only at the end.

MA.q: A newborn weighed 3.2 kilograms at birth and 3.65 kilograms at a two-week checkup. Use 1 ounce = 28 grams. To the nearest whole ounce, how much weight did the newborn gain?

n.0: This treats the 0.45 kg gain as 0.45 lb (7.2 oz) without converting kilograms.
n.1: This treats 0.45 kg as 45 g; 1 kg = 1,000 g, so the gain is 450 g.
n.2: This converts 0.45 kg to 4,500 g by moving the decimal point four places (4,500 ÷ 28 = 160.7); 1 kg = 1,000 g.

MA.q: If 4/9 = x/63, what value of x makes the two fractions equivalent?
MA.w: 63 ÷ 9 = 7, so the denominator was multiplied by 7. Multiply the numerator by 7 too: 4 × 7 = 28. Check by cross-multiplying: 4 × 63 = 252 and 9 × 28 = 252.

n.1: 36 multiplies the old numerator by the old denominator (4 × 9) instead of by the multiplier 7.
n.2: 7 is the multiplier (63 ÷ 9), not the new numerator; the numerator 4 still has to be multiplied by it.
n.3: 58 adds 54 to the numerator because 54 was added to the denominator; adding the same number does not keep the value.

MA.q: Solve for x: (3/4)x - 5 = 13.
MA.w: Add 5 to both sides: (3/4)x = 18. Multiply both sides by the reciprocal 4/3: x = 18 × 4/3 = 24. Check: (3/4)(24) - 5 = 18 - 5 = 13.

n.0: This multiplies 18 by 3/4 instead of by its reciprocal, 4/3.
n.2: This multiplies 18 by 4 but does not divide by 3. Multiplying by 4/3 does both.
n.3: Sign error: 5 was subtracted from 13 instead of added, giving (3/4)x = 8.

MA.q: A home health aide drives 2 5/6 miles to one client and 3 3/4 miles to the next. What is the total distance in miles?

n.0: 6 5/12 renames 5/6 as 8/12 instead of 10/12, giving 17/12.
n.1: 5 7/12 drops the 1 whole carried from 19/12.
n.3: 5 4/5 adds the numerators and the denominators of the fractions: (5 + 3)/(6 + 4) = 8/10.

MA.q: A bottle holds 250 mL of a liquid medication. The prescribed dose is 7.5 mL twice a day. How many full days will the bottle last?
MA.w: Daily use: 7.5 × 2 = 15 mL. Days: 250 ÷ 15 = 16.67. Only complete days count, so round down to 16 days (16 × 15 = 240 mL).

n.0: This rounds 16.67 up. After 16 days only 10 mL is left, which is not enough for both doses on day 17.
n.1: This is the number of full doses (250 ÷ 7.5), not days; there are 2 doses per day.
n.2: This rounds the number of doses (33.3) up and treats each dose as a day.

MA.q: Nia takes out a $6,500 loan for nursing school at 4.8% simple annual interest for 3 years. What is the total amount she will repay, including interest?

n.0: This charges interest for 1 year only: 6,500 + 312.
n.1: This compounds the interest each year. Simple interest uses I = P × r × t on the original $6,500 only.
n.3: This is the interest alone; the total repaid also includes the $6,500 borrowed.

MA.q: Which Roman numeral has the greatest value?
MA.w: CDXC = 490; CDXCIX = 499; DIX = 509; CCCXCIX = 399. DIX is the greatest.

n.1: CDXCIX = 400 + 90 + 9 = 499; reading CD as 600 makes it look larger than 509.
n.2: CCCXCIX = 300 + 90 + 9 = 399, which is less than 509.
n.3: CDXC = 400 + 90 = 490, which is less than 509.

MA.q: The prescribed amount of a medication is 4 mg per kilogram of body weight. A patient weighs 165 pounds. Using 1 kg = 2.2 lb, how many milligrams should be given?

n.1: This multiplies by 2.2 instead of dividing (165 × 2.2 × 4). Pounds to kilograms makes the number smaller.
n.2: This uses the weight in pounds (4 × 165) without converting to kilograms.
n.3: This is the weight in kilograms; it still has to be multiplied by 4 mg per kg.

MA.q: Which list orders 2/3, 3/5, 5/8 and 7/12 from greatest to least?

n.0: This ranks the fractions by denominator, smallest first; 5/8 = 0.625 is greater than 3/5 = 0.6.
n.2: This ranks the fractions by numerator (7, 5, 3, 2), not by value.
n.3: This is least to greatest (ascending), the reverse of the order asked.

MA.q: A pharmacist divides 2 1/4 ounces of a compounded cream into small tubes that each hold 3/16 ounce. How many tubes can be filled? Enter the number of tubes only.

tr.10: Divided only the whole number 2 by 3/16 (10 2/3) and dropped the 1/4 ounce.

MA.q: Which expression has a negative value?
MA.w: -4² means -(4 × 4) = -16, which is negative. The exponent applies only to 4, not to the negative sign.

n.1: (-4)² = 16; the parentheses include the sign, and two negative factors give a positive.
n.2: (-2)³ = -8, and -8 × (-3) = 24, which is positive.
n.3: -3 × (-5) = 15; two negatives multiply to a positive.

MA.q: A 100 mL bag of solution is divided equally into 8 syringes. How many milliliters go into each syringe?
MA.w: 100 ÷ 8 = 12 R 4. As a decimal the remainder is 4/8 = 0.5, so each syringe gets 12.5 mL. Check: 8 × 12.5 = 100.

n.0: 1.25 mL places the decimal point one place too far left; 8 × 1.25 = 10, not 100.
n.2: 12.04 mL writes the remainder 4 in the hundredths place; the remainder is 4/8 of a milliliter.
n.3: 12.4 mL writes the remainder 4 as the decimal digits; 4 left over out of 8 is 0.5, not 0.4.

MA.q: A blood bank collected 1,487 units in May, 2,056 in June and 968 in July. How many units did it collect in all?
MA.w: Ones: 7 + 6 + 8 = 21, write 1, carry 2. Tens: 8 + 5 + 6 + 2 = 21, write 1, carry 2. Hundreds: 4 + 0 + 9 + 2 = 15, write 5, carry 1. Thousands: 1 + 2 + 1 = 4. Total 4,511.

n.0: 3,543 adds only May and June and leaves out July.
n.1: 3,511 forgets the 1 carried into the thousands place.
n.3: 4,501 carries 1 instead of 2 from the ones column (21).

MA.q: Which pair of quantities is in an inverse proportion?
o: The miles driven and the gallons of gas used at a steady fuel economy
The hours worked and the pay earned at a fixed hourly wage
The number of nurses sharing a fixed workload and the hours it takes
The number of 250 mg tablets given and the total milligrams given
MA.w: In an inverse proportion the product stays constant: doubling the number of nurses on a fixed workload halves the hours. The other pairs increase together (direct proportion).

n.0: Miles and gallons increase together at a constant rate, so this is a direct proportion.
n.1: Pay grows at a constant rate as hours increase, so this is a direct proportion.
n.3: Each extra tablet adds 250 mg, so the total grows with the count: a direct proportion.

MA.q: A patient in a cardiac rehabilitation program walks 1 mile in 16 minutes at a steady pace. What is the patient's walking speed in feet per second?

n.0: 330 is the speed in feet per minute (5,280 ÷ 16); divide by 60 to get feet per second.
n.1: This divides seconds by feet (960 ÷ 5,280), which gives seconds per foot.
n.3: 3.75 is the speed in miles per hour (60 ÷ 16), not feet per second.

MA.q: Solve for x: 5(x - 2) = 3(x + 4).
MA.w: Distribute: 5x - 10 = 3x + 12. Subtract 3x: 2x - 10 = 12. Add 10: 2x = 22. Divide by 2: x = 11. Check: 5(9) = 45 and 3(15) = 45.

n.0: Sign error when moving -10: the right side becomes 12 + 10 = 22, not 12 - 10 = 2.
n.1: This adds 3x to the left side instead of subtracting it, giving 8x - 10 = 12, so 8x = 22.
n.2: This distributes to the x terms only, giving 5x - 2 = 3x + 4, so 2x = 6.

MA.q: An ambulance travels 42 miles in 35 minutes. What is its average speed in miles per hour?
MA.w: 35 minutes = 35/60 hour. Speed = 42 ÷ (35/60) = 42 × 60 ÷ 35 = 72 miles per hour.

n.1: This treats 35 minutes as half an hour (42 ÷ 0.5).
n.2: This rounds 35/60 = 0.583 to 0.6 hour before dividing (42 ÷ 0.6). Round only at the end.
n.3: This writes 35 minutes as 0.35 hour. Thirty-five minutes is 35/60 of an hour.

n.0: 9 3/16 multiplies 21/4 × 7/4 without flipping the divisor.
n.2: 5 1/3 divides the parts separately (5 ÷ 1 = 5 and 1/4 ÷ 3/4 = 1/3); convert to improper fractions first.
n.3: 1/3 flips the first fraction instead of the divisor (4/21 × 7/4).

MA.q: A travel nurse worked 38.5, 41.2, 39.8, 40.6 and 39.1 hours over five weeks. Which is the best estimate of the total number of hours she worked?
MA.w: All five values cluster near 40, so estimate 5 × 40 = 200 hours. (Exact: 199.2 hours.)

n.0: 160 counts four weeks (4 × 40) instead of five.
n.2: 220 rounds every value up to the next ten (40 + 50 + 40 + 50 + 40) instead of to the nearest ten.
n.3: 170 truncates each value to the tens place (30 + 40 + 30 + 40 + 30) instead of rounding.

MA.q: A 12-ounce bag of coffee makes 45 cups. At the same rate, how many cups can be made from a 32-ounce bag? Enter the number of cups.

tr.65: Added the 20-ounce difference to 45 instead of scaling.
tr.8.53: Set up the second ratio upside down (12 × 32 ÷ 45).

MA.w: Set up 12/45 = 32/c. Cross-multiply: 12c = 1,440, so c = 120 cups.

MA.q: The scale on a trail map is 2 centimeters to 0.5 kilometer. A hike measures 13 centimeters on the map. What is the actual length of the hike?
MA.w: Set up 2/0.5 = 13/d. Cross-multiply: 2d = 6.5, so d = 3.25 kilometers. (1 cm represents 0.25 km, and 13 × 0.25 = 3.25.)

n.1: This multiplies 13 by 2 and leaves out the 0.5 km.
n.2: This sets up the proportion upside down, multiplying 13 by 2 ÷ 0.5.
n.3: This multiplies 13 by 0.5 as if 1 cm represented 0.5 km; it is 2 cm that represents 0.5 km.

MA.q: What is CX minus XLIV, written as a Roman numeral?
MA.w: CX = 110 and XLIV = 44. 110 - 44 = 66 = LXVI.

n.0: This reads IV as 6, so XLIV becomes 46 and 110 - 46 = 64.
n.1: This reads XLIV as 66 by adding every symbol (110 - 66 = 44).
n.3: This reads XL as 60, so XLIV becomes 64 and 110 - 64 = 46.

MA.q: A child's liquid antibiotic dose is 1 1/2 teaspoons twice a day. The bottle holds 4 fluid ounces. Use 1 fluid ounce = 30 milliliters. How many full days will the bottle last at this dose?
MA.w: Dose = 1.5 × 5 mL = 7.5 mL; per day = 2 × 7.5 = 15 mL. Bottle = 4 × 30 = 120 mL. 120 ÷ 15 = 8 days.

n.1: This counts one dose per day (120 ÷ 7.5); the dose is given twice a day.
n.2: This uses 15 mL per fluid ounce; the stem gives 1 fl oz = 30 mL.
n.3: This uses 15 mL per teaspoon, which is the tablespoon amount; 1 tsp = 5 mL.

MA.q: A clinic gave 640 flu shots in October and 512 flu shots in November. What was the percent decrease in flu shots from October to November?
MA.w: Change = 640 - 512 = 128. Percent change = 128 ÷ 640 × 100 = 20% decrease.

n.1: This is November's total as a percent of October's, not the percent decrease.
n.2: This divides the change by the new value, 512. Percent change divides by the original value, 640.
n.3: This turns the 128-shot drop into a percent without dividing it by the original value.

MA.q: A nursing class has 45 students. 1/3 attend the morning section, 2/5 attend the afternoon section, and the rest study online. How many students study online?

n.0: 15 is the morning section (1/3 of 45), not the online group.
n.1: 33 is the number in the two classroom sections (15 + 18), one step short of the answer.
n.2: 18 is the afternoon section (2/5 of 45), not the online group.

MA.q: Over one week, a patient's daily walks added up to 34/12 miles. Which mixed number, written in simplest form, is equal to 34/12?
MA.w: 34 ÷ 12 = 2 with a remainder of 10, so 34/12 = 2 10/12. Simplify the fraction part by dividing both terms by 2: 2 5/6.

n.0: 3 1/6 = 38/12. It rounds the quotient up to 3 and uses 36 - 34 = 2 as twelfths.
n.2: This halves the numerator of 10/12 but not the denominator, which changes the value.
n.3: 2 10/12 equals 34/12, but the fraction part is not in simplest form.

MA.q: One patient's dressing is changed every 4 days and another's IV site every 6 days. Both were done today. In how many days will both next fall on the same day?
MA.w: The next shared day is the least common multiple of 4 and 6. Multiples of 4: 4, 8, 12; multiples of 6: 6, 12. LCM = 12 days.

n.0: 2 is the greatest common factor of 4 and 6, not the least common multiple.
n.1: 10 adds the two intervals; the schedules meet at a common multiple.
n.3: 24 multiplies 4 × 6, a common multiple but not the least; both fall together on day 12 first.

MA.q: In the number 52.0847, which digit is in the thousandths place?
MA.w: Right of the point: 0 tenths, 8 hundredths, 4 thousandths, 7 ten-thousandths. The thousandths digit is 4.

n.0: 0 is in the tenths place, the first place after the point.
n.2: 7 is in the ten-thousandths place, the fourth place after the point.
n.3: 8 is in the hundredths place, the second place after the point.

MA.q: A lab technician multiplies two measurements and gets a product of 0.0024. Which multiplication gives a product of exactly 0.0024?
MA.w: 4 × 6 = 24. In 0.04 × 0.06 the factors have 2 + 2 = 4 decimal places, so the product is 0.0024.

n.1: 0.004 × 0.06 has 5 decimal places in total, so the product is 0.00024.
n.2: 0.4 × 0.06 has 3 decimal places in total, so the product is 0.024.
n.3: 0.4 × 0.6 has 2 decimal places in total, so the product is 0.24.

MA.q: An account holds $412.50. A deposit of $86.25 is made, then payments of $129.40 and $57.08 clear. What is the balance?

n.0: $369.35 subtracts only the first payment.
n.1: $139.77 subtracts the deposit instead of adding it.
n.2: $312.37 forgets to reduce the tenths digit after borrowing in 369.35 - 57.08.

AP.q: During fetal development, most bones form by replacing a hyaline cartilage model. Which bone instead forms directly within a fibrous membrane by intramembranous ossification?
AP.w: Intramembranous ossification builds bone directly in a fibrous membrane: the flat bones of the skull, the clavicles and some facial bones. Long bones and vertebrae form by endochondral ossification, replacing a hyaline cartilage model.

n.0: The humerus is a long bone that forms by endochondral ossification from a cartilage model.
n.1: Vertebrae are irregular bones that form by endochondral ossification from cartilage models.
n.2: The femur is a long bone that forms by endochondral ossification from a cartilage model.

AP.q: A patient asks how she will digest fat after her gallbladder is removed. Which explanation is most accurate?
o: Her pancreas will take over storing bile
Her stomach digests most fat, so bile is less needed
Her liver still makes bile that reaches the duodenum
Her small intestine will make the lipase it once supplied
AP.w: The liver, not the gallbladder, makes bile. Without a gallbladder, bile from the liver still drains into the duodenum to emulsify fat; it is simply not stored and concentrated between meals.

n.0: The pancreas makes pancreatic juice and does not store bile.
n.1: Most fat digestion happens in the small intestine, not the stomach.
n.3: The gallbladder never supplied lipase; lipase comes from the pancreas.

AP.q: Standing in a cold wind, a hiker begins to shiver. Which statement best explains how shivering helps maintain body temperature?
o: Dermal blood vessels dilate, carrying warm blood out to the skin
Cardiac muscle beats faster, and its extra contractions make the heat
Smooth muscle in vessel walls contracts rhythmically and releases heat
Skeletal muscles contract involuntarily, releasing heat as they use ATP
AP.w: Shivering is rapid, involuntary contraction of skeletal muscle triggered by the hypothalamus. Much of the energy released as the muscles use ATP is lost as heat, so heat production rises and body temperature is maintained. Constriction of dermal vessels conserves heat but does not produce it.

n.0: Dilation of dermal vessels sends warm blood to the surface and releases heat; in the cold these vessels constrict to conserve it.
n.1: A faster heartbeat is not shivering; shivering is repeated contraction of the large mass of skeletal muscle, which is the main source of the extra heat.
n.2: Shivering is contraction of skeletal muscle, not vascular smooth muscle; narrowing of dermal vessels conserves heat but is not shivering.

AP.q: When blood pressure suddenly rises, stretch receptors in large arteries signal the brain, which then slows the heart rate. Which statement correctly identifies the type of feedback and the heart's role?
o: Positive feedback; the heart acts as the effector
Negative feedback; the heart acts as the receptor
Negative feedback; the heart acts as the effector
Positive feedback; the heart acts as the control center
AP.w: Two steps. Slowing the heart reverses the rise in pressure, so this is negative feedback (the baroreceptor reflex). The heart carries out the response directed by the brain, so it is the effector.

n.0: The heart is the effector, but the response opposes the rise in blood pressure, which is negative feedback.
n.1: This is negative feedback, but the receptors are the stretch receptors in the arteries; the heart produces the response.
n.3: The response opposes the change (negative feedback), and the control center is the brain, not the heart.

AP.q: The stomach wall has a lining that secretes mucus, layers that contract to churn food, nerves that coordinate the contractions, and a layer that binds these together. Which statement explains why the stomach is classified at the organ level?
o: It works with the esophagus and intestines to digest food
Its wall combines two or more tissue types working together
It contains several cell types, all within its mucus lining
Its lining cells are specialized to secrete mucus and acid
AP.w: The mucus-secreting lining is epithelial tissue, the contracting layers are muscle tissue, the nerves are nervous tissue and the binding layer is connective tissue. Two or more tissue types working together make an organ, and the stomach has all four.

n.0: Cooperating with other organs is what places the stomach in an organ system (the digestive system); it does not explain why the stomach itself is an organ.
n.2: Several cell types within one layer can still be a single tissue, as in blood. An organ needs two or more tissue types.
n.3: Specialized cells describe the cellular or tissue level. Specialization alone does not make a structure an organ.

AP.q: During weeks of ongoing stress before final exams, which hormone sustains Mei's long-term stress response by raising blood glucose and suppressing inflammation?
AP.w: Cortisol, a glucocorticoid from the adrenal cortex, drives the long-term stress response: it raises blood glucose by gluconeogenesis, is anti-inflammatory and suppresses immunity.

n.1: Cortisol is the right hormone, but it comes from the adrenal cortex, not the medulla.
n.2: Epinephrine from the adrenal medulla drives the short-term, fight-or-flight response, not weeks of sustained stress.
n.3: Aldosterone from the adrenal cortex controls Na⁺ and K⁺ and blood volume, not glucose or inflammation.

AP.q: A drop in blood pressure triggers the release of renin, the first step in a chain that raises blood pressure again. Which statement about renin is correct?
o: It is an enzyme in the lungs that forms angiotensin II
It is an enzyme from juxtaglomerular cells of the kidney
It is a hormone secreted by the adrenal cortex
It is a hormone from the heart atria that lowers pressure
AP.w: Renin is an enzyme released by juxtaglomerular cells of the kidney when blood pressure or sodium is low. It converts angiotensinogen into angiotensin I.

n.0: Angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE), found mostly in the lungs, forms angiotensin II; renin acts earlier.
n.2: The adrenal cortex releases aldosterone later in the pathway; renin comes from the kidney.
n.3: ANP from the atria lowers blood pressure; renin is part of the system that raises it.

AP.q: Insulin is often injected into the hypodermis. Based on its word parts, where is this layer located?
AP.w: hypo- means below and derm/o means skin, so the hypodermis (subcutaneous layer) lies beneath the dermis.

n.0: Within the dermis would be intradermal (intra- within).
n.2: Around would use peri-; the hypodermis is a layer below the dermis, not a wrapping.
n.3: The layer above the dermis is the epidermis (epi- upon).

AP.q: A clinic handout reviews the jobs of the digestive organs that food does not pass through. Which of the following functions is carried out by the liver?
AP.w: The liver converts toxic ammonia from protein breakdown into urea, which the kidneys then excrete. It also makes bile, stores glycogen, detoxifies drugs and alcohol, and makes plasma proteins.

n.1: The gallbladder stores and concentrates bile; the liver makes it.
n.2: Insulin and glucagon come from the islets of the pancreas, its endocrine part.
n.3: Trypsinogen is made by the acinar cells of the exocrine pancreas.

AP.q: During a panic attack, a student breathes rapidly and deeply for several minutes. Using CO₂ + H₂O ⇌ H₂CO₃ ⇌ H⁺ + HCO₃⁻, what happens in her blood?
o: CO₂ builds up, the reaction shifts right, H⁺ rises and pH falls
CO₂ is blown off, the reaction shifts left, H⁺ falls and pH rises
CO₂ is blown off, the reaction shifts right, H⁺ rises and pH falls
CO₂ is blown off, the reaction shifts left, H⁺ falls and pH falls
AP.w: Step 1: hyperventilation removes CO₂ faster than it is made. Step 2: with less CO₂, the equilibrium shifts left, using up H⁺; fewer H⁺ ions means a higher pH (respiratory alkalosis).

n.0: CO₂ builds up with slow, shallow breathing, not with rapid deep breathing.
n.2: Removing a reactant (CO₂) shifts the equilibrium left, not right, so H⁺ falls.
n.3: The shift and the fall in H⁺ are right, but fewer H⁺ ions means pH rises.

AP.q: A patient with type A blood is mistakenly given type B red blood cells and has a transfusion reaction. What causes the reaction?
o: Her anti-B antibodies bind the B antigens on the donor red cells
Her plasma lacks antibodies, so the donor B antigens attack her cells
Her anti-A antibodies bind the A antigens on the donor red cells
Her A antigens bind directly to the B antigens on the donor red cells
AP.w: Step 1: type A blood has A antigens on the cells and anti-B antibodies in the plasma. Step 2: donor type B cells carry B antigens, so her anti-B antibodies bind them and destroy the donor cells.

n.1: Type A plasma does contain antibodies (anti-B), and antigens are markers, not attackers.
n.2: Type A blood does not contain anti-A antibodies (they would attack her own cells), and type B cells carry no A antigen.
n.3: Antigens do not bind one another; antibodies bind antigens.

AP.q: Small glands on the posterior surface of the thyroid secrete a hormone that raises blood calcium. Which choice names the glands and the hormone?
AP.w: The parathyroid glands, usually four on the back of the thyroid, secrete parathyroid hormone (PTH), which raises blood calcium by releasing it from bone, keeping it in the kidneys and activating vitamin D.

n.0: The thymus, in the mediastinum, secretes thymosin for T-cell maturation; it does not regulate calcium.
n.1: Thyroid C (parafollicular) cells secrete calcitonin, which lowers blood calcium; they are part of the thyroid itself.
n.3: The glands are right, but calcitonin comes from the thyroid and lowers calcium; the parathyroids secrete PTH.

AP.q: A charting guide lists four example sentences that use proximal or distal. Which sentence uses one of these terms correctly?
o: The fingers are proximal to the palm
The knee is proximal to the ankle
The wrist is proximal to the elbow
The heart is distal to the stomach
AP.w: Proximal means closer to where a limb attaches to the trunk. The knee is closer to the hip than the ankle is, so the knee is proximal to the ankle.

n.0: The fingers are farther from the limb's attachment than the palm, so they are distal to the palm.
n.2: The wrist is farther from the shoulder than the elbow is, so the wrist is distal to the elbow.
n.3: Proximal and distal describe limbs and branching structures. Organs of the trunk are compared with superior/inferior or anterior/posterior.

AP.q: Each eye has a small blind spot where the optic nerve leaves the retina at the optic disc. Why does no image form at this point?
o: It contains rods but no cones
It contains cones but no rods
It is covered by the opaque sclera
AP.w: The optic disc has no photoreceptors (no rods or cones), so light falling on it cannot be detected.

n.1: A region with rods would still detect light in black and white; the optic disc has neither rods nor cones.
n.2: Cones without rods describes the fovea centralis, the point of sharpest vision; the optic disc has neither rods nor cones.
n.3: The sclera is the white outer layer of the eyeball; it does not cover the inner surface of the retina.

AP.q: The pancreas releases digestive enzymes through a duct into the small intestine and also releases insulin directly into the bloodstream. Which classification of the pancreas is correct?
o: An endocrine gland, because its enzymes act as hormones in the blood
Both an exocrine and an endocrine gland, with ducted and ductless parts
An exocrine gland, because insulin also leaves the gland through a duct
An endocrine gland, because a gland making any hormone is endocrine
AP.w: Exocrine glands secrete through ducts onto a surface (the pancreatic enzymes), and endocrine glands are ductless and secrete hormones into the blood (insulin). The pancreas does both.

n.0: Digestive enzymes travel through a duct to the small intestine; they are exocrine secretions, not hormones.
n.2: Insulin is a hormone released directly into the blood without a duct, which is an endocrine function.
n.3: Making a hormone shows endocrine function, but the pancreas also secretes enzymes through a duct, so it is exocrine as well.

AP.q: Before helper T cells can respond to a new pathogen, other cells must display fragments of the pathogen's antigens on MHC proteins. Which cells perform this antigen presentation?
o: Helper T cells and cytotoxic T cells
Plasma cells and natural killer cells
AP.w: Antigen-presenting cells (dendritic cells, macrophages and B cells) take in antigens and display fragments on MHC proteins so that T cells can recognize them.

n.0: T cells are the cells that recognize presented antigen; they are not the antigen-presenting cells.
n.1: Mast cells and basophils release histamine in inflammation and allergy; they are not antigen-presenting cells.
n.3: Plasma cells secrete antibodies and NK cells kill infected cells; neither presents antigen to T cells.

AP.q: A patient with severe liver failure has a low blood albumin level and bleeds easily from minor cuts. Which loss of liver function best explains both findings?
o: Reduced conversion of ammonia to urea
AP.w: The liver makes plasma proteins, including albumin and clotting factors such as fibrinogen and prothrombin. Losing this function explains both the low albumin and the easy bleeding.

n.1: Glycogen storage affects blood glucose control, not albumin or clotting.
n.2: Failing urea production raises blood ammonia; it does not lower albumin or impair clotting.
n.3: Less bile could reduce fat-soluble vitamin absorption, but it would not explain the low albumin.

AP.q: Which cranial nerve carries visual signals away from the retina, and which lobe of the cerebrum processes these signals?
AP.w: Two steps: the optic nerve (CN II) carries visual signals from the retina, and vision is processed in the occipital lobe.

n.0: CN III is a motor nerve to the eye, and the parietal lobe processes touch and body position.
n.1: The occipital lobe is right, but CN III moves the eye and constricts the pupil; it does not carry visual signals.
n.3: The nerve is right, but the temporal lobe processes hearing, not vision.

AP.q: When Priya looks up from her phone to a distant sign, the shape of her lens changes to keep the image focused on the retina. Which structures change the lens shape?
o: Muscles moved by the abducens nerve
AP.w: The ciliary muscles change the shape of the lens so it can focus light from near or distant objects on the retina.

n.0: The choroid is the vascular layer of the eye; it does not change the shape of the lens.
n.1: The muscles of the iris change pupil size, not lens shape.
n.3: The abducens nerve (CN VI) moves the eyeball laterally; it does not focus the lens.

AP.q: A stroke damages the region of the brain that generates the basic rhythm of breathing. Which region is damaged?
AP.w: The respiratory centers in the medulla oblongata set the basic breathing rhythm; the pons helps smooth the pattern.

n.0: The hypothalamus regulates temperature, hunger and thirst; it does not generate the breathing rhythm.
n.1: The pons modifies and smooths the breathing pattern, but the basic rhythm is generated in the medulla.
n.2: The cerebellum coordinates movement and balance; it is not a breathing center.

AP.q: Which valve lies between the heart chamber with the thickest myocardium and the largest artery of the body?
AP.w: The left ventricle has the thickest myocardium, and the aorta is the largest artery. The aortic semilunar valve guards the exit from the left ventricle into the aorta.

n.0: The tricuspid valve lies between the right atrium and the right ventricle.
n.2: The pulmonary valve guards the exit from the thinner-walled right ventricle into the pulmonary trunk.
n.3: The mitral valve sits at the entrance to the left ventricle, between it and the left atrium, not at its exit.

AP.q: A patient with a bacterial infection develops a moderate fever. Which statement best describes how the fever arises and how it helps the body?
o: Histamine resets the hypothalamic set point, and moderate heat activates memory cells
Pyrogens reset the hypothalamic set point, and moderate heat inhibits pathogens
Pyrogens reset the pituitary set point, and moderate heat inhibits pathogens
Pyrogens reset the hypothalamic set point, giving an antigen-specific adaptive defense
AP.w: Fever is an innate, nonspecific second-line defense. Pyrogens released during infection reset the temperature set point in the hypothalamus, and a moderate rise in body temperature inhibits pathogens.

n.0: Pyrogens, not histamine, reset the set point; histamine drives local inflammation, and memory cells belong to adaptive immunity.
n.2: The body's temperature set point is in the hypothalamus, not the pituitary.
n.3: Fever is innate and nonspecific; it does not target one antigen the way adaptive immunity does.

AP.q: Years of smoking destroy many of the cilia that line a patient's bronchi. Which normal airway function is most directly impaired?
o: Sweeping mucus and trapped particles up toward the pharynx
Producing mucus from goblet cells to trap inhaled dust
Warming and humidifying air as it passes over the conchae
Secreting surfactant to keep the alveoli from collapsing
AP.w: Cilia on the airway epithelium beat to move the mucus sheet, with its trapped particles, up toward the pharynx (the mucociliary escalator). Without cilia, mucus pools and is cleared by coughing.

n.1: Mucus is made by goblet cells, not cilia, so mucus is still produced; it is moving it that fails.
n.2: Warming and humidifying occur mainly in the nasal cavity, over the vascular mucosa of the conchae, not by bronchial cilia.
n.3: Surfactant is secreted by type II alveolar cells, which have no cilia.

AP.q: Besides T3 and T4, the thyroid gland secretes a third hormone from its parafollicular (C) cells. Which hormone is it, and what does it do?
o: Parathyroid hormone; it raises blood calcium
AP.w: The parafollicular (C) cells of the thyroid secrete calcitonin, which lowers blood calcium by favoring bone deposition and reducing osteoclast activity.

n.1: The hormone is right, but calcitonin lowers blood calcium; PTH raises it.
n.2: Thymosin is made by the thymus, not by the thyroid gland.
n.3: Parathyroid hormone is made by the parathyroid glands on the back of the thyroid, not by thyroid C cells.

AP.q: A surgeon reviews the location of the kidneys before a kidney procedure. Which statement about kidney position is correct?
o: They lie behind the peritoneum, the right slightly lower
They lie inside the peritoneal cavity, the right slightly lower
They lie inside the peritoneal cavity, the left slightly lower
They lie behind the peritoneum, the left slightly lower
AP.w: The kidneys are retroperitoneal, at about T12 to L3. The liver sits above the right kidney, so it lies slightly lower than the left. The adrenal glands sit on top of the kidneys.

n.1: The right kidney is lower, but the kidneys are retroperitoneal, not inside the peritoneal cavity.
n.2: Both parts are wrong: the kidneys are retroperitoneal, and the right one sits lower because of the liver.
n.3: The kidneys are retroperitoneal, but the right kidney, not the left, sits lower because the liver lies above it.

AP.q: During an all-out 400-meter sprint, lactic acid builds up in a runner's leg muscles. Which process produces this lactic acid?
o: Glycolysis when oxygen supply is short
Hydrolysis of ATP by myosin heads
AP.w: When oxygen delivery cannot meet demand, pyruvate from glycolysis is converted to lactic acid. Anaerobic glycolysis is fast but yields 2 ATP per glucose.

n.0: Creatine phosphate donates its phosphate to ADP, leaving creatine; it does not form lactic acid.
n.2: Myosin's hydrolysis of ATP yields ADP and phosphate to power the stroke; it does not form lactic acid.
n.3: Aerobic respiration needs oxygen and produces carbon dioxide and water, not lactic acid.

AP.q: After a fall, Diego has damage confined to his cerebellum. Which problem is he most likely to show during his recovery?
o: Loss of control of breathing rhythm
Loss of balance and poorly coordinated movement
Inability to regulate body temperature and thirst
AP.w: The cerebellum coordinates movement and controls balance and posture, so damage to it produces unsteady, poorly coordinated movement.

n.0: Breathing rhythm is set by the medulla oblongata, with help from the pons, not the cerebellum.
n.1: Understanding spoken language depends on Wernicke's area in the temporal lobe.
n.3: Body temperature and thirst are regulated by the hypothalamus.

AP.q: Six primary oocytes and six primary spermatocytes complete meiosis normally, and each oocyte is fertilized so that meiosis II finishes. How many ova and how many sperm result in total?
AP.w: Two steps. (1) Oogenesis divides the cytoplasm unequally, so each primary oocyte yields 1 ovum plus polar bodies: 6 x 1 = 6 ova. (2) Spermatogenesis yields 4 sperm per primary spermatocyte: 6 x 4 = 24 sperm.

n.1: This counts 2 sperm per spermatocyte, which stops after meiosis I; meiosis II gives 4 per spermatocyte.
n.2: This treats oogenesis like spermatogenesis; polar bodies are not functional ova, so each oocyte gives 1 ovum.
n.3: This counts the first polar body as a second ovum; polar bodies degenerate and are not ova.

AP.q: A patient is lying face down on an exam table, and a nurse notes a bruise on the back of the right thigh, the surface facing the ceiling. Which term correctly describes the bruised surface of the thigh?
o: Lateral, because that surface faces away from the exam table
Superior, because the bruise faces upward while the patient lies prone
Anterior, because the bruise is on the surface farthest from the table
Posterior, because terms are based on anatomical position
AP.w: Directional terms are defined by anatomical position no matter how the patient is lying. The back of the thigh is posterior.

n.0: Lateral means away from the midline of the body, not away from a table. The back of the thigh is its posterior surface.
n.1: Superior means toward the head in anatomical position, not toward the ceiling in the patient's current position.
n.2: Anterior is the front of the body. The back of the thigh stays posterior when the patient lies face down.

AP.q: A blood sample is drawn from a pulmonary artery and compared with a sample from a pulmonary vein. How does the pulmonary artery sample differ?
o: It has the same oxygen, since both vessels serve the lungs
It has higher oxygen and lower carbon dioxide
It has higher oxygen and higher carbon dioxide
It has lower oxygen and higher carbon dioxide
AP.w: Step 1: the pulmonary artery carries blood from the right ventricle to the lungs, before gas exchange. Step 2: the pulmonary vein carries blood after exchange. So the arterial sample is lower in O₂ and higher in CO₂ (the classic exception to the oxygen rule).

n.0: Gas exchange in the lung capillaries lies between the two vessels, so their oxygen content differs.
n.1: This would be true of a systemic artery compared with a systemic vein, but the pulmonary artery carries deoxygenated blood.
n.2: Blood that is high in CO₂ has not yet unloaded it in the lungs, so its O₂ is low as well.
